the energy storage properties of the investigated (Pb, La, Sr) (Zr, Sn, Ti) O3 ceramics can be tailored via the substitution of titanium for tin.
the maximum dielectric constants and the energy density increased with increasing titanium content.
the dielectric constant increased, the temperature of the maximum dielectric shift to lower values, and the energy storage properties improved as the titanium content increased.

the effect of titanium content on dielectric properties and energy storage properties in the (Pb, La, Sr) (Zr, Sn) TiO3 ceramics.
the effects of the titanium content on the dielectric and energy density properties of (Pb0.88La0.04)(Zr0.65Sn0.35)O3 ceramics.
the effect of titanium content on the dielectric and energy density properties of lead lanthana strontium zirconate stannate ceramics.

the dielectric and energy-storage properties of the ceramics could be tailored to some extent by the titanium content.
the increase of the titanium content in (Pb, La, Sr)(Zr, Sn, Ti)O3 ceramic is favorable to enhance the dielectric properties and energy storage performance.
the dielectric and energy-storage properties of the ceramics can be tailored by controlling the titanium content.

the increase in titanium content in the (Pb, La, Sr)(Zr, Sn, Ti)O3 ceramics is favorable to the enhancement of the energy storage properties.

the dielectric and energy density of (Pb0.90La0.04)(Zr0.65Sn0.30Ti0.05)O3 ceramics can reach 2,500 pF/cm and 0.6 J/cm3, respectively, with a high discharge power of 2.4 GW/cm3.
